Asha: Heads-up  small doc cleanup for Optimize toolkit. I noticed three examples under /optimize that still use old quant profile keys and one caching snippet that assumes auto-prefetch is on by default. Opening a single PR to: fix keys, add an explicit prefetch example, and tweak the batching heuristics paragraph for clarity. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4957 :memo:
Ben: Thanks  can you list the specific files?
Asha: Sure: /optimize/quant/profiles.md (YAML uses q_profile_old), /optimize/batching/heuristics.md (text ambiguous about batch_size recommendations), examples/snippets/cache-prefetch.py (implicit prefetch), examples/snippets/quant-examples.yaml (old key names).
Liu: For the prefetch snippet, can we show both the explicit warmup call and a note about TTL on cached KV entries? People often assume it's permanent.
Asha: Good call. I'll add a tiny Python snippet showing client.prefetch(model, max_tokens=1024) with context and a note: "cache TTL defaults to 6h; set prefetch.TTL to override."
Ben: Also add a short migration note at top of profiles.md: "q_profile_old renamed to q_profile_2024. Old names continue to work for now but may be deprecated." That's customer-facing and prevents confusion.
Liu: When you change batching heuristics, can you include an explicit example of adjusting batch_size per route? Many apps want a per-endpoint override example.
Asha: Yes, adding a config block that shows route -> batching.profile: short-seq vs long-seq and example token distribution guidance.
DocsBot: Auto-note: PR 4957 created by Asha. Docs CI queued: link-checker, yaml-lint.
Ben: Quick ask: add a short Node snippet too for prefetch and mention Node 18+ for for-await streaming.
Asha: Will do. Goal is one tidy PR to avoid scatter. Planning to land by Friday if reviews are green.
Liu: I'll grep the repo for old profile keys and post any extras here so you can include them in the same change.
Asha: Thanks  appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
